results.claim: Corollary 3.8 gives the one-way implication J^{d,n} hyperbolic => P^{d,n} hyperbolic, per instance; the document states it as 'never the converse' and calls P 'a strictly weaker condition carrying the same equivalence' to RH.
results.paper_quote: "Corollary 3.8. If J^{d,n}(x) is hyperbolic then P^{d,n}(x) is hyperbolic." (Sect. 3.2; proof via Cor. 3.7 applied to the reciprocal x^d J^{d,n}(1/x).) The paper states only this implication.
results.doc_quote: "carries the same equivalence to RH (Theorem 1.2) under a strictly weaker condition (Corollary 3.8: J hyperbolic then P hyperbolic)"; "The implication is one-way"; "the implication is confirmed on all 35 cells, not that the converse fails".
results.notes: The core implication is verbatim the paper (numbering matches v2). The added 'never the converse' / strictness is NOT in O'Sullivan: the paper proves J=>P only and never asserts the converse fails. The document itself concedes its 35 cells test only where J holds, which cannot refute J. In the archive the 'converse does not hold' wording traces to another harvested file (xihorn-h-track-os-corollary-3-8.md:18), and the only published converse remark in the neighborhood is GOR+ Remark (3), not O'Sullivan. If 'never the converse' is meant literally it is false at d=2 (Gamma(n+1)^2+2Gamma(n)^2 >= Gamma(n)Gamma(n+2) can hold while the Turan inequality fails).

results.claim: Theorem 1.3: P_{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic once n/log^2 n >= d^{3/4}/2, for d large; the document also states this replaces the exponential onset of GOR+ Theorem 1.1 ('n >= c*e^d', exponent 0.9634) with a polynomial bound.
results.paper_quote: "Theorem 1.3. For all d sufficiently large, P^{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic whenever n/log^2 n >= d^{3/4}/2." (Sect. 1.) Proof in Sect. 8 uses Turan's Thm. III (Thm. 8.1), condition (8.2), Lemma 8.2 with c=2.
results.doc_quote: "both bound the onset only asymptotically ... n/log^2 n >= d^{3/4}/2 for P ([O'S] Theorem 1.3, 'd large')"; "[O'S] Theorem 1.3 then replaces the exponential with a polynomial: P_{d,n} is hyperbolic once n/log^2 n >= d^{3/4}/2, for d large."
results.notes: Numbering, inequality and the d-large qualifier all match v2 as read. Detail: 'd large' is the document's paraphrase; the paper's words are 'For all d sufficiently large'. The paper's own comparison target is GOR+ Theorem 1.1 at n >> e^{8d/9} (exponent 8/9 = 0.889), not the 0.9634 the document quotes for 'their proof'; that 0.9634 figure is about the GOR+ paper, which was not fetched in this batch, so it is unchecked here rather than wrong.

results.claim: Theorem 1.4 gives the Lambert-W asymptotic for gamma(n) with w := W(2n/pi); every c_k is described through the chain B-hat_{i,j} (2.1), l_i (2.6), a_r (7.4), mu_r (7.7), kappa_m (7.11), kappa*_k and c_k (7.13); Table 1 gives gamma(1000) = 4.8450426112725879772e-2568.
results.paper_quote: "Theorem 1.4. Set w:=W(2n/pi). Then as n->infty we have gamma(n)=4pi^2 e^{7w/4} sqrt(w/(w+1)) (ew^2/(16 n e^{2/w}))^n (1+ sum_{k=1}^{K-1} c_k(w)/n^k + O(log^K(n)/n^K))"; "The coefficients c_k(w) are completely described by the formulas (2.6), (7.4), (7.7), (7.11) and (7.13)."
results.doc_quote: "The paper describes every c_k, through a chain of five formulas - (2.6) l_i, (7.4) a_r, (7.7) mu_r, (7.11) kappa_m, (7.13) kappa*_k and c_k, all built on the partial ordinary Bell polynomials B-hat_{i,j} of (2.1)."
results.notes: Formula, numbering and the five-formula chain match v2 verbatim (the paper spells the chain out at Sect. 7, just after the proof of Thm. 1.4). c_1 is (1.8); c_2 is printed as an 8th-degree rational function as the document says. kappa_m = 1, 1/12, 1/288, -139/51840, -571/2488320 is the classical Stirling series consistent with (7.11). Table 1's last row is exactly 4.8450426112725879772 x 10^-2568, matching the document's answer key. No overreach found.

results.claim: Theorem 3.5: for Phi(z) = sum c_j z^j/j! real entire of genus 1* and any Omega in the Laguerre-Polya class, Phi hyperbolic iff sum_{j=0}^{d} C(d,j) c_j g*_{d-j}(Omega;x) is hyperbolic for all d >= 1; Omega=1 gives J^{d,n}, Omega=e^{-z^2} gives P^{d,n}(x/2).
results.paper_quote: "Theorem 3.5. Let Phi(z)=sum_{j=0}^{infty} c_j z^j/j! be a real entire function of genus 1* and let Omega(z) be in the Laguerre-Polya class. Then Phi(z) is hyperbolic if and only if the polynomials sum_{j=0}^{d} C(d,j) c_j g*_{d-j}(Omega;x) (3.5) are hyperbolic for all d >= 1."
results.doc_quote: "for Phi(z) = sum c_j z^j/j! real entire of genus 1* and any Omega in the Laguerre-Polya class, Phi hyperbolic <=> sum_{j=0}^{d} C(d,j) c_j g*_{d-j}(Omega; x) hyperbolic for all d >= 1"; "Omega = 1 gives J^{d,n}; Omega = e^{-z^2} gives P^{d,n}(x/2)."
results.notes: Statement, hypotheses (genus 1*, Omega in LP, all d >= 1) and numbering match v2 exactly; the paper also uses the word 'any' ('may be used to give different criteria ... introducing an interesting flexibility'). The Omega=1 and Omega=e^{-z^2} substitutions are the paper's own, including the shift: the paper notes g*_d(Theta^(n) . e^{-z^2};x) = sum C(d,j) gamma(j+n) H_{d-j}(x/2) = P^{d,n}(x/2) (3.6), so the document's 'P^{d,n}(x/2)' is right. The document's further gloss that this substitution is what moved the effective bound from e^{0.96d} to d^{3/4}log^2 n is the archive's own reading of the paper's introduction comparison, not a claim of Theorem 3.5.

results.claim: Corollary 3.2 localized to a fixed shift: xi^(n) is hyperbolic iff J_{d,n} is hyperbolic for every d >= 1, where 'xi is the Riemann xi function; xi^(n) its n-th derivative'.
results.paper_quote: "Corollary 3.2. The function Theta^{(n)}(z) is hyperbolic if and only if J^{d,n}(z) is hyperbolic for all d >= 1." Its proof: "We know that Theta(z) is real and entire of order 1/2. All of its derivatives ... implies that Theta^{(n)}(z) is real and entire of genus 1* for all n >= 0."
results.doc_quote: "**Fixed n, all d.** [O'S] Corollary 3.2: xi^(n) is hyperbolic <=> J_{d,n} is hyperbolic for every d >= 1." / "xi is the Riemann xi function; xi^(n) its n-th derivative."
results.notes: The numbered result exists and its right-hand side (J_{d,n}, all d >= 1) is right, but the left-hand side is not what the paper states. O'Sullivan's corollary is about Theta^{(n)}, the n-th derivative of Theta(z) := xi(1/2+sqrt(z)), a different function from the n-th derivative of xi. The proof needs Theta real and of order 1/2, hence genus 1*; xi(s) is complex on the real axis and is not hyperbolic in the paper's sense at all, so the document's biconditional is not even well posed as written. The paper never states any result about xi^{(n)}. Only the numbering (3.2) was checked against v2.

results.claim: Corollary 3.8 is quoted as a strict per-instance comparison: J_{d,n} hyperbolic => P_{d,n} hyperbolic, 'never the converse', with the converse claimed to fail.
results.paper_quote: "Corollary 3.8. If J^{d,n}(x) is hyperbolic then P^{d,n}(x) is hyperbolic." (Sect. 3.2.) That is the whole statement; no converse, no strictness, and no claim that P can hold where J fails.
results.doc_quote: "And the per-instance comparison is strict ([O'S] Corollary 3.8: J_{d,n} hyperbolic => P_{d,n} hyperbolic, never the converse)." / "the source says it is strict - the converse never holds."
results.notes: The implication and its numbering (3.8) are faithful, but 'never the converse' and 'strict' are added by the archive and are absent from the paper. At d = 2 the paper's own display shows the P-condition is the J-condition plus the free positive term 2gamma(n)^2, which at best makes the P-condition easier to satisfy, not provably strictly easier. The document admits in its notes that the source does not print the corollary's wording and reproduces no proof; it also concedes elsewhere (xihorn-todo-os-corollary-3-8.md:23) that the 35 tested cells do not show the converse fails. Numbering matches v2.

results.claim: Lemma 3.4 identifies (3.5) as g*_d(Phi.Omega; x), so 'every choice of Omega is the classical Jensen family of the product Phi.Omega', and multiplying by an LP factor neither adds nor removes real-zero content.
results.paper_quote: "Lemma 3.4. Let Phi and Omega be two formal power series with Phi(z)=sum_{j=0}^{infty} c_j z^j/j!. Then for all d >= 0 g*_d(Phi.Omega;x)=sum_{j=0}^{d} C(d,j) c_j g*_{d-j}(Omega;x). (3.3) Proof. This is an easy exercise."
results.doc_quote: "Lemma 3.4 identifies (3.5) as g*_d(Phi.Omega; x): every choice of Omega is the classical Jensen family of the product Phi.Omega, and multiplying by an LP factor neither adds nor removes real-zero content."
results.notes: The identification itself is right: (3.3) is exactly what makes (3.5) equal g*_d(Phi.Omega;x), and it is used that way in the proof of Thm. 3.5. But Lemma 3.4 as printed is a bare algebraic identity for any two formal power series - no Laguerre-Polya hypothesis, no hyperbolicity, no real-zero claim. The real-zero half of the document's sentence belongs to the proof of Theorem 3.5 and requires Omega in LP: "The zeros of Omega are real since it is in the Laguerre-Polya class. Therefore Phi.Omega is in the Laguerre-Polya class if and only if Phi(z) is hyperbolic." Attributing it to Lemma 3.4 drops that hypothesis. Numbering (3.3)/(3.5) matches v2.
